objects.taxonomy_description: Cylindrical stick of wax (15-30 cm tall, 2-5 cm diameter) with a central wick (cotton string) extending from the top. The wax body is smooth and uniform, available in white, ivory, or colored varieties. The surface has a matte or slightly glossy finish depending on wax type (paraffin, beeswax, soy). The top has a charred wick tip if previously burned. Taper candles narrow toward the top; pillar candles maintain uniform diameter. The base is flat for standing. Scented candles may have a slightly textured surface from fragrance oils. The overall shape is a simple vertical cylinder with a thin wick protruding from the center.

objects.taxonomy_description: Equine mammal measuring 140-170 cm at withers with athletic build. Coat uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coloration with no black points. Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen). Head elongated with large expressive eyes and mobile ears. Neck arched and muscular. Body deep-chested with strong back. Legs long and slender with single hoof per foot. Tail long with flowing hair. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse body hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Color variant of horse distinguished by reddish-brown coat.

objects.taxonomy_description: Large gregarious predatory feline of Africa and India with a distinctive tawny coat. Males have a prominent shaggy mane ranging from blonde to dark brown surrounding the head and neck. Coat is short, dense, and uniform tawny with a lighter underside. Body is large, muscular, and well-proportioned with powerful legs and a long tail with a dark tuft at the end. Head is broad with a short muzzle. Ears are small, rounded, and erect. Eyes are medium-sized, round, and amber to brown with an intense expression. The breed's signature features include the male's distinctive mane, social pride behavior, and tawny coat with tail tuft.
